facts.text: Montgomery was founded in 1835 by Daniel Gray, who built the first wooden house there in 1836 and later named the village after his New York county.
In 1858 the village of Montgomery was officially incorporated, with Ralph Gray, Daniel’s son, elected its first president.
The 1990 Montgomery Historical Committee book, “The History of Montgomery, Illinois in Words and Pictures,” was so popular it was reprinted twice and again in 2014 with a grant‑funded update.
Montgomery’s early industry included a stationary engine factory and a stone grain mill known as the Gray–Watkins Mill, both founded by Daniel Gray.
The Aurora Caterpillar plant on Montgomery’s southern border has been building wheel‑loaders there since 1959.
Montgomery sits roughly 45 miles southwest of Chicago, straddling southern Kane and northern Kendall counties within the Chicago Metropolitan Area.
